processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Hot-rolled at 1050–950 °C to a 6 mm sheet then air cooled to room temperature.
Single-stage heat treatment at 1000 °C for 3 min followed by quenching to room temperature (state designated S1000).

structures.overall_structure: Full austenitic matrix with elongated stripe-like Cr7C3 precipitates distributed along the austenite grain boundaries, annealing twins, and nanoscale κ-carbides co-gridded within the austenite; effective grain size 3.17 μm with 71.7 % special (Σ≤29) grain boundaries.

phases_present.texture: main misorientation peak near 60° (Σ3 annealing twins)

phases_present.volume_fraction: cannot be accurately measured (κ-carbide, B2, and Cr7C3 content could not be accurately measured)
phases_present.morphology: elongated stripe-like precipitates on austenite grain boundaries

grain_structure.texture: Σ3-twin dominated; special boundaries (Σ≤29) 71.7 % of grain boundary length; main misorientation peak near 60°

precipitates.size: elongated stripe-like (morphology); no numeric size reported

defect_interactions.interaction_type: intergranular crack nucleation at grain-boundary precipitates
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Cracks nucleate preferentially at grain boundaries due to Cr7C3; cracks generally follow the RHAGBs under further deformation extension; the special boundaries in S1000 have limited effect on changing crack propagation or deflection.

interfaces.slip_behavior: Impact-fracture micrographs of S1000 show quasi-cleavage planes with slip bands, likely caused by large numbers of dislocations moving along the quasi-cleavage plane; microcracks and microvoids observed where slip-band interaction is significant.
interfaces.phase_evolution: Cr7C3 present at grain boundaries in S1000; as temperature is increased to 1050 °C the Cr7C3 dissolves on the grain boundary (not for S1000).
interfaces.interface_notes: The Cr7C3 at S1000 grain boundaries causes intergranular fracture characteristics; grain boundaries are apparent with no obvious deformation (characteristic of intergranular fractures).

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: Tensile: gauge length 25 mm, gauge width 4 mm, gauge thickness 5 mm; Impact: standard Charpy V-notch 5 mm × 10 mm × 55 mm
measurement_conditions.test_standard: standard Charpy V-notch impact test (5 mm × 10 mm × 55 mm)
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile specimens fabricated along the rolling direction; properties are averages of three tests for each condition; yield strength determined as 0.2 % offset strength; tests at room temperature.

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Fig. 4(a) engineering stress–strain curve; Fig. 4(b) true stress–strain and strain-hardening-rate curves (S1000 red curve)
strain_hardening_rate: strain-hardening rate drops sharply at very low strain, rises to a hump peaking near 2000 MPa at strain interval 0.20–0.22, then decreases (three stages I, II, III)

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: standard Charpy V-notch 5 mm × 10 mm × 55 mm

service_conditions.stress_state: tensile loading and Charpy impact loading (room temperature mechanical testing)

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: impact energy (toughness): S1000 is the lowest of the three conditions (88.6 % below MHT)

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: cross-sectional specimens mechanically polished and etched with 40 ml HNO3 + 100 ml ethyl alcohol
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterize matrix microstructure, grain-boundary precipitates and twins; examine tensile fracture and impact fracture surfaces
characterization_methods.key_findings: S1000 shows austenitic equiaxed grains with twins and elongated stripe-like Cr7C3 precipitates along austenite grain boundaries; tensile fracture shows non-uniform dimples.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: EBSD probe on Zeiss Ultra 55 FESEM
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: EBSD specimens chemically polished with colloidal silica without etching; average grain size including twin boundaries measured via intercept lengths; Σ≤29 classified as special boundaries
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure effective grain size, misorientation angle distribution and proportions of Σ boundaries/special boundaries
characterization_methods.key_findings: S1000 effective grain size 3.17 μm; 71.7 % special boundaries (Σ≤29); main misorientation peak near 60° (Σ3 twins).

characterization_methods.technique: transmission electron microscopy (TEM) with selected area electron diffraction (SAED)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: TEM specimens 0.5 mm thick ground to 80 μm, electrochemically polished in twin-jet apparatus with 10 % perchloric acid + 90 % methanol
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify phase composition of precipitates (κ-carbide, Cr7C3) and their orientation relationships
characterization_methods.key_findings: S1000 contains nano-scale κ-carbide (3–10 nm) co-gridded with austenite ([011]γ // [011]κ) and elongated stripe-like Cr7C3 on the austenite grain boundaries (SAED zone axis [11-2-]Cr7C3).

characterization_methods.technique: energy dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) in SEM mode
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: C content in austenite calculated from lattice parameter equations (1) and (2) because EDS is unreliable for C
characterization_methods.purpose: Determine austenite chemical composition (Mn, Al, Ni, Cr, C)

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: constant strain rate 3 mm/min; gauge length 25 mm, width 4 mm, thickness 5 mm; average of three tests
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure yield strength, ultimate tensile strength, total elongation and stress-strain behaviour

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: standard Charpy V-notch specimens (5 mm × 10 mm × 55 mm) at ambient temperature; average of three tests
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure impact absorbed energy and separate crack initiation and crack propagation energies via load-displacement curves
characterization_methods.key_findings: S1000 lowest impact energy 29.2 J; crack propagation energy 9.87 J; displacement 4.55 mm.

computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated grain-boundary strengthening uses measured effective grain size (3.17 μm) and Hall-Petch constant K = 461 MPa·μm^(1/2); σ_PPT = σ_YS − σ_0 − σ_GR yields 209 MPa for S1000.

analytical_models.model_name: Yield strength superposition: σ_YS = σ_0 + σ_GR + σ_PPT
analytical_models.equation_role: Decompose yield strength into lattice friction/solid-solution, grain-boundary and precipitation contributions

parameters.name: σ_0 (lattice friction + solid-solution strengthening) for S1000
σ_0 formula: σ_0 = 97 + 279 wt% C + 1.5 wt% Mn + 20.5 wt% Al + 2.9 wt% Ni + 3.9 wt% Cr

analytical_models.model_note: Because the κ-carbide, B2, and Cr7C3 contents could not be accurately measured, σ_PPT was obtained as σ_YS − σ_0 − σ_GR; S1000 strengthening is dominated by solid-solution strengthening.

unmapped_findings: S1000 impact behaviour (instrumented Charpy): total absorbed energy 29.2 J comprises crack initiation energy and crack propagation energy; crack propagation energy is 9.87 J and the load-displacement displacement is 4.55 mm (lowest of the three conditions).
S1000 austenite composition measured by EDS (Table 2), wt.%: Mn 20.97 ± 0.34, Al 9.30 ± 0.02, Ni 2.04 ± 0.26, Cr 3.24 ± 0.78, C 1.17 ± 0.13, Fe Bal.
Cube-austenite/κ-carbide orientation relationship for S1000: [011]γ // [011]κ (κ-carbide co-gridded with austenite, additional faint superlattice diffraction spots in SAED).

Cr7C3 on the grain boundaries of S1000 causes preferential crack nucleation at grain boundaries (aggregated micropores), and cracks generally follow the random high-angle boundaries; the special boundaries in S1000 have limited effect on changing crack propagation or deflection, giving intergranular fracture characteristics.

S1000 impact fracture surface shows quasi-cleavage planes with slip bands, microcracks and microvoids; the shear zone area of S1000 is the smallest of the three conditions (larger shear zone correlates with better toughness).

The paper reports sample density of the alloy as 6.78 g/cm³ (drainage method, ~14 % lower than pure iron 7.87 g/cm³) for the base ingot, applicable to the studied alloy rather than to a specific heat-treatment state.
